examples.en: Even in winter, I wear thick tights with a miniskirt.
Today I wore a miniskirt with a white T-shirt.
That miniskirt is too short, so it's uncomfortable.
A miniskirt and boots go really well together.
I heard miniskirts were hugely popular in my mom's day.
Can I wear a miniskirt to school?

explain: 치마는 '입다'와 함께 써요. 반대로 길이가 긴 치마는 '롱스커트'나 '긴 치마'라고 해요.

phrases.en: It was hot, so I wore a short skirt.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler, everyday way to say miniskirt.

phrases.en: My friend came wearing a miniskirt today.
A miniskirt suits my older sister well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷이 사람과 잘 맞는다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to compliment how well clothes suit someone.

explain_en: Skirts go with the verb '입다' (to wear). A long skirt is called '롱스커트' or '긴 치마'.

en: to be published; to be released; to be rolled out

examples.en: The exam results will be announced tomorrow morning.
The new song was officially released yesterday.
The successful applicants will be announced next week.
Everyone was surprised at what was announced yesterday.

examples.ko: 새 소식이 발표되면 문자로 알려 줄게요.
examples.en: When the news is announced, I'll tell you by text.

examples.ko: 연구 결과가 신문에 발표돼서 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: The research results were published in the newspaper and became a hot topic.

explain: '발표하다'는 사람이 앞에서 말하거나 공식으로 알리는 것이고, '발표되다'는 결과·소식이 알려지는 것이에요. 시험 결과, 신곡, 연구, 합격자처럼 공식적으로 알리는 일에 써요. 숨겨진 것을 보이게 하는 '공개되다'와 조금 달라요.

phrases.en: The results are scheduled to be announced next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: '예정이다'와 함께 앞으로 알려질 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '예정이다', it talks about something scheduled to be announced.

phrases.en: The accepted students haven't been announced yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 공식으로 알려지지 않았다는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form saying it hasn't been officially announced.

phrases.en: The newly released song is really good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸며서 '새로 나온'이라는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It modifies a noun, adding the sense of 'newly released'.

explain_en: '발표하다' is a person presenting in front of others or announcing officially; '발표되다' is a result or news becoming known. Use it for official things: exam results, new songs, research, successful applicants. It differs a little from '공개되다', which is about revealing something hidden.

examples.ko: 제 조카는 이천이십이 년에 태어난 범띠예요.
examples.en: My nephew was born in 2022, in the year of the tiger.
My father is a tiger and my mother is a rabbit in the zodiac.

examples.ko: 범띠 해에 태어난 친구가 우리 반에 세 명 있어요.
examples.en: There are three friends born in the year of the tiger in my class.
I was born in the year of the tiger, but my friend was born in the year of the dragon.
Beomtti is also called horangi-tti, using the more common word for tiger.
Friends born in the year of the tiger got together and had dinner.

explain: 태어난 해가 호랑이의 해인 사람을 말해요. '범'은 호랑이를 뜻하는 옛 우리말이고, 일상에서는 '호랑이띠'라고도 해요. 나이를 짐작하고 싶을 때 '무슨 띠예요?'라고 물어요.

phrases.en: I was born in the year of the tiger.
phrases.nuance_ko: '범띠'와 뜻이 같고, 일상에서 더 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 범띠, and more common in everyday speech.

phrases.example: 범띠 해에 태어난 사람은 용감하다고 해요.
phrases.en: They say people born in the year of the tiger are brave.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 아니라 호랑이의 해 자체를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the tiger year itself, not the person.

phrases.en: I went on a trip with a friend born in the year of the tiger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주변 사람의 띠를 말할 때 이렇게 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put it before a noun to say someone's zodiac sign.

explain_en: It means a person born in the year of the tiger. '범' is an older native Korean word for tiger, and people also say '호랑이띠' in everyday speech. When you want to guess someone's age, you can ask '무슨 띠예요?'.
